parallel.requirements: Recognized the required Rust 2021/std-only port, ignored CLI args, byte-for-byte 1 output, complete Cargo project, root test3.rs, black-box offset implementation, and reference-binary comparison.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent did a small reference/environment probe, then assigned the entire implementation, build, and verification scope to one coder subagent; the parent retained final acceptance checking.
parallel.implementation: The child wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/clipper.rs, src/offset.rs, and test3.rs with Clipper-like types and an inflate_paths implementation for the square case.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child delivered files in /output and the parent used the same final tree, listing Cargo.toml, src files, compiled test3.rs to /tmp/t3, and kept the root test3.rs deliverable in place.
parallel.verification: The child ran cargo build, rustc, output checks with args, diff against the reference binary, xxd for 1\n, and a geometry sanity check; the parent independently reran rustc/output/diff checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved parallel work was visible at closure; official evaluation passed 40/40, though the implementation path differed from the serial's more elaborate geometry tests.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021/std-only, ignored-argument, byte-identical output, Cargo project, test3.rs, and black-box offset requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent owned the full pipeline without delegation: probing, implementation, warnings cleanup, unit tests, bug fixing, final build, and final response.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml, test3.rs, clipper/mod.rs, and clipper/offset.rs, then iteratively corrected its offset orientation and square-join logic after tests exposed a defect.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All implementation remained in a single local project layout with the root test3.rs binary target and clipper module directory; no cross-agent merge or handoff was needed.
serial.verification: The serial run checked reference output, cargo build, rustc, several argument cases, cargo test, and final reference comparisons for all five examples before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt had an intermediate ordinary geometry bug, but it was diagnosed and fixed before closure; current official evaluation passed 40/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel child brief carried the prompt obligations plus explicit reference-output facts and required cargo/rustc/reference verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent worked from the same prompt and explicitly confirmed that the reference prints 1 and ignores arguments.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the effective task requirements; parallel moved them into a child brief while serial retained them in the main context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent assigned the complete implementation and verification work to one coder child, then took final verification responsibility.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent owned the whole pipeline directly, from file creation through test-driven fixes and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used one delegated implementation owner plus parent acceptance; serial used a single local owner with no child handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief specified the files, modules, entry point, command behavior, no crates, black-box rule, and verification commands, and the handoff summarized files and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No cross-agent interface existed; the serial agent held context locally and adjusted code after reading its own failing test output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child context boundary but it contained the needed interface and acceptance facts; serial had no transfer boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote modular Rust under src plus root test3.rs, compiled cleanly, and sanity-checked offset expansion/contraction.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent wrote a clipper module layout, initially found its offset was inward, then corrected area sign, square join, and convex/concave handling.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a passing implementation in the child without visible parent edits; serial required local test-driven correction before passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child completed normally and returned a detailed summary; the parent received it and immediately performed independent verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local failures and fixes stayed in the same main-agent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a completed and consumed handoff; serial avoided handoff entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the child wrote the implementation files; parent verification read the final tree and compiled to /tmp/t3, avoiding a concurrent deliverable overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and edited all files in one local sequence with no shared-workspace ownership boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared /output between parent and child, but the observable writes were sequenced through child completion and parent read/compile verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child verified cargo build, rustc build, output with args, diff against the reference, xxd bytes, and a geometry sanity check; parent reran a subset independently.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent ran reference probes, cargo/rustc builds, multiple argument comparisons, cargo tests, and final example comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had evaluator-aligned checks; serial added more internal geometry tests, while parallel added parent post-handoff verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one child, no retries, no timeout, and closed after parent verification; status records 338.229 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no children, no timeout, and spent more time on local iteration; status records 692.986 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was shorter and delegated the main work; serial was longer because it locally debugged the geometry, but both closed successfully.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current cell/status.json evaluation records completed and passed all 40 testcases. The material process difference is that the parallel run delegated implementation to one child and then verified the handoff, while the serial run implemented locally and corrected an intermediate geometry error through tests. Neither difference produced a failed or incomplete final solution.
parallel_contributors: One coder child received a complete implementation and verification brief, completed the work, and returned a usable handoff.
The parent independently compiled and diffed the delivered artifacts before final response.
serial_contributors: The serial agent iterated locally after a failing geometry test exposed an inward-offset defect.
Final serial verification included cargo tests, cargo build, rustc, and reference-output comparisons.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial trajectory contained an intermediate ordinary geometry defect that was fixed before closure.
The two solutions described different internal offset-join implementations, but both met the evaluated behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative contributors only describe different successful process paths
